venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: The score was 66–21. The film is two jobs. Faulkner kept FAU off Baugh. White moved Woods. The short throw stayed open, and FAU ran ninety plays.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — compressed, no yardage nicknames. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Faulkner’s job is to keep you from deciding the ball is going to Baugh. White’s job is to keep the tackle from knowing who has the outside. One held. One left the short throw on the grass.

offense.body:
You cannot put a card on this offense. That is the point.

Faulkner does not install a system you can memorize. He asks a new question before you finish the last one. Same start. Different answer. They can still go the other way without changing the play.

If you creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. First man misses. Brown scores from 49 yards. People will remember a long touchdown. It was a short throw and a missed tackle.

If you follow the tackles who look like they are leading a run, the ball goes the other way — Brown, with the three linemen in the middle already out in front. Later it is Clark. Same picture. On his touchdown those big people are already down the field.

If you stay put and play Baugh, he runs it. He scores from 12 with those linemen actually leading him this time. In the third quarter everybody knows it is Baugh, and he still rips off 61 yards.

That is one idea. He keeps changing the picture.

Receivers way out wide. Brown and Wilson one behind the other. FAU crowds Baugh because they have seen him. That leaves Brown or Wilson alone with half the field. One miss and he is gone. That is Brown’s night. Not a trick. Just room.

More players on one side. A man in motion. FAU still counting when the ball is snapped. Not decoration. That is how Faulkner plays the numbers.

The fake run is the lie and the truth. Sometimes the tackles leave and the ball goes with the three in the middle — Brown, later Clark. Sometimes those tackles really are leading Baugh and he walks into it. When they need one yard, nobody leaves — sneak, Philo from the 3.

They will also have a tackle take off like it is a run when they are passing. The rusher has to choose: chase Philo or honor the fake. Either way he is late. Week one they showed it more than they got a big play out of it. They will hand it off from that same look.

Philo with Baugh right behind him showed up once — they ran it, then they faked it and Wilson sat in the open grass for 19 yards. One look. Not the offense. Wilson moved the chains because he sits in the grass you leave him.

Philo ran the offense. In and out. Eyes down when they rushed him. Step up, still find somebody. He does not have to be the hero. Stockton walked in from the 11 on a ball that was a little late. When FAU finally crowded Baugh, the line looked like pass and Philo threw it over the top to Abrams — 63 yards. Lead him a step and he walks in. The pick is Mays. The ball came off his hands. Sweeney was sitting. When Philo holds it, the play dies.

Baugh is the night. Fourteen carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores, including that 61-yarder. FAU filled every hole on some plays — extra people, nowhere to go — and he still ripped it. That is not scheme. That is the best player in the building. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven on him. Receivers out wide make that a nightmare. Clark is the change of pace. They will not run Baugh thirty times.

The line is clean — almost no penalties, no late-shift disaster like last year. They are not getting out to the linebackers fast. The wide run is not ready. Faulkner still shows it so you have to worry about the outside. His move: do not ask this line to block everybody. Leave people unblocked on purpose.

The snaps over Philo’s head are Moore’s hands. Sumrall already said it. The one that lost twenty yards inside the five is the kind that loses real games. Philo ran it himself once, FAU’s end was still there, lost two yards. Idea fine. Play lost.

They block down the field like they mean it. A ten-yard run becomes thirty. Micah Jones blows up one man, then the next, and they throw him the last touchdown. Same idea as Clark’s score — a big person in front of a skill player.

Saturday was a coordinator who flexes to what you are weak at, a back you cannot tackle if they do not put extra men on him, and a quarterback who ran the offense. Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays. The rest is a headache.
bullets: You creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. Brown scores from 49.
You follow the fake, the ball goes the other way — Brown, later Clark.
You stay put, Baugh runs it — including 61 yards when everybody knew.
Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
FAU wants the short throw until you take it away. Florida never took it away.

Corners lined up yards off. Linebackers not standing where that short ball lands. You show them something before the snap and give them the same throw after it. Ninety plays. Ten of thirteen on third down. Henry and Valsin lived on the five-to-eight yard catch. Sumrall said it: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened. That is the tax.

White will live with the short throw if they tackle. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody stood where the ball lands, so FAU kept moving the chains.

He still has a real idea. He moves people. Woods is how he does it. On third down he shifts him. Sometimes Woods is rushing from the outside. Sometimes he walks inside and someone else has that outside rush. The tackle never knows who is coming. Mix it. Often.

When Veltkamp holds it, the idea pays. Coleman acts like the middle is open, the ball goes outside, Coleman is already there. That pick is bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Johnson goes up and gets it. Same idea. Bett beats the quarterback at the 1, ball out, Johnson falls on it. McCloud wins fourth-and-2. The rush finally finishes.

Safeties were clean — Coleman, Thornton. Clark played a real night in the slot and lost one ball to the corner of the end zone with no help. That throw is the cost of lining up yards off. Valsin scored from 20. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What leaked is the stuff inside the plan. The pile at the 1 — they had enough people, they lost the yard. The man on the outside left and Veltkamp walked in from 7. Woods has to stay there. When he chases, FAU runs at him.

Later they sent four rushers and still played the corners off. That kills the deep ball. It also leaves the short throw and the throw to the corner alive.

They were ready for how fast FAU plays. They were not staring at the sideline when it snapped. Veltkamp is a real quarterback — he can throw it and run it. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety plays and those fourth downs are what you get when the short throw is free.

Stand where the short ball lands. Keep Woods on the outside when the quarterback runs it. Mix Woods. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: The short throw was open. That is why FAU ran 90 plays.
White moves Woods so the tackle never knows who is coming.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it.
Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

specials.body: Durkin from 53. Clean. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt starts Florida’s second score.

keys: Faulkner never lets you sit on Baugh. You creep up — Brown. You follow the fake — the ball goes the other way. You play it straight — Baugh runs it.
Receivers out wide force a choice: extra men on Baugh, or room for Brown.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot settle. FAU moved the chains because the short throw was free.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it. Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and keep changing the picture. White has to stand on that short throw and keep Woods on the outside when Sixkiller runs it himself.
